title: Decoupled traffic adapter for cross-mode canary/A-B/shadow orchestration
creator: Aisha Park
description: Implement a decoupled traffic adapter that translates a single deployment intent (canary, A/B, shadow) into concrete routing and capacity operations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments. The adapter should enforce environment-specific constraints (e.g., tenancy, KMS availability, bandwidth/egress caps, GPU shape compatibility) and produce a deterministic execution plan with preflight validation and simulated promotion outcomes. Goal: enable unified lifecycle tooling without leaking environment assumptions into callers or requiring mode-specific rollout recipes.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts a single canonical rollout spec and emits per-environment routing actions and validations
Preflight validator rejects plans that violate private/VPC constraints (missing KMS, unavailable GPU family) with actionable diagnostics
Automated promotion simulator produces 95th-percentile latency and cost delta estimates for candidate canary sizes
Shadow traffic plumbing can mirror up to 30% synthetic traffic to Dedicated pools without impacting production SLOs (configurable throttle)
Auto-rollback triggers when canary error rate or quality metric breach thresholds and executes environment-safe rollback within 2 minutes
End-to-end integration test coverage for hosted->dedicated and hosted->private canary flows
Documentation pages and console UI knobs surfaced for traffic split, rollback thresholds, and promotion windows
tasks: Design translation schema for canonical rollout spec -> environment actions (lead: Marcus)
Implement preflight constraint checker and improved diagnostic messages (lead: Farah Khan)
Build traffic adapter modules: hosted-router, dedicated-proxy, private-bridge (parallel work)
Integrate with autoscaler to reserve burst capacity for canaries in Dedicated
Add simulation harness that replays recent traffic to estimate cost/latency impact
Wire auto-rollback hooks into rollout controller with safe-ordering for Private environment
Create integration test matrix and run with synthetic tenants across regions
Write Console feature page and CLI docs; add e2e runbook for operators
decisions: Use a canonical rollout spec (YAML) that encodes traffic fractions, metric gates, and promotion schedule; adapter maps this to per-mode capabilities
Adapters must be idempotent and emit a dry-run plan with resource reservations; apply stage only after explicit confirmation or policy auto-approve
For Private deployments, adapter will prefer blue-green over in-place canaries when KMS or HSM constraints exist
Shadow traffic will be implemented using non-blocking mirrors with tokenized headers to avoid telemetry contamination
Auto-rollback will run a two-phase guard: immediate traffic cut (fast path) then graceful model re-promotion if safe
Simulation uses synthetic replay at current QPS distribution; we will not mirror sensitive PII in tests—use anonymized payloads
notes: Constraint taxonomy drafted: capacity (GPU, memory), networking (egress, region), security (KMS/HSM, audit logs), policy (tenant isolation), cost (burst budget)
Mapping table between canonical ops and environment primitives exists in doc but needs normalization (see link below)
We must coordinate with Platform Security for Private KMS key onboarding; estimate onboarding lead time 3 weeks for new tenants
Dedicated pools currently expose a limited set of GPU flavors; adapter will surface fallbacks and quantization recommendations where necessary
Quality gates should include a signal from Redwood Optimize (regression detector) in addition to latency/error metrics
